facts: The verification layer is the cryptographic backbone of MotoPass — it proves data integrity without requiring trust in the platform.
Every verification starts with a SHA-256 hash of the data: the hash is the fingerprint, not the data itself.
The Satohash API accepts a 64-hex SHA-256 hash and anchors it into a Bitcoin transaction via OpenTimestamps (OTS) calendars.
A stamp starts as 'pending' and becomes 'confirmed' when a Bitcoin block includes the OTS anchor — the block height is the proof.
Polling (GET /api/stamps/:id) checks the anchor status; terminal statuses are confirmed, anchored, complete, failed, error, rejected.
The Verify page (/verify) supports four modes: generate+stamp, OTS paste/file upload, batch hash verification, and hash history re-verification.
Batch verification processes one SHA-256 hash per line, validates format, and offers Satohash deep links for each.
OTS paste verification parses hex-dump or base64 OTS file content for structural checks (browser-side cannot do full OTS verify).
Full OTS verification requires either the Satohash server or the opentimestamps Node.js CLI — the browser does structural validation only.
Hash history is stored in localStorage (max 5 entries) so users can re-verify previous hashes without re-entering them.
The proof lifecycle is: hash locally → submit to Satohash API → poll for Bitcoin anchor → confirm block height → announce on Nostr (optional).
When program data changes (daily intel pipeline), proofs are re-stamped: the old proof stays in audit_trail, the new one is anchored.
Re-stamping follows pacing rules: 2-second delay between stamps, max 15 per run, to respect Satohash API rate limits.
proof.in_sync in intel.json reports whether a program's proof matches its current canonical slice — honest per-program state.
Document stamping (Vault) hashes the file locally via crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256'), submits only the hash, never the file.
The shared document registry (localStorage) is the single source of truth across Profile, Vault, and Dashboard pages.
Each registry entry has: id, name, size, type, hash, stampId, status (pending/confirmed/error), blockHeight, createdAt, updatedAt.
deriveDocStatus() maps API status strings to honest statuses: confirmed/anchored/complete → confirmed; failed/error/rejected → error; else pending.
restampHash() re-submits an existing hash to the Satohash API without needing the original file — the hash is the anchor.
refreshStampStatus() re-checks a stored document's anchor against the API — used by the Dashboard quick-action button.
The Verify page checks Satohash API health on mount via GET /health — shown as online/offline badge in the page header.
When the Satohash API is offline, the stamp button falls back to a deep-link guide URL (satohash.io/stamp?hash=<hash>).
Nostr attestation is optional and fire-and-forget: a kind 30078 replaceable event is built, signed via NIP-07, and published to relays.
The Nostr event carries tags: hash, satohash URL, stamp-id, block height, stamp-status — all allowlisted and sanitized.
signedEventMatchesTemplate() ensures the NIP-07 signer did not swap kind, tags, or content — prevents rogue signer mutation.
validateTimestampTemplate() checks: kind is 30078, hash tag is 64-hex, satohash URL is allowlisted, stamp-id passes regex, OTS path is relative.
The allowlisted Satohash origins are: satohash.io, api.satohash.io, satohash.giveabit.io — enforced by isAllowedSatohashUrl().
Page verification (/verify?path=<route>&build=<id>) hashes the current route + build ID for deploy-integrity checks.
buildPageVerifyPayload() creates a canonical JSON payload from pathname + buildId + platform, which is then SHA-256 hashed.
The document registry export (motopass-document-registry/v1) includes per-document verify_url for offline auditing against Bitcoin.
Registry import validates schema, requires 64-hex hashes, preserves backup statuses as claims, and offers re-check for honest confirmation.
mergeRegistryBackup() deduplicates by id, keeps the newer updatedAt, and sorts newest-first — safe for idempotent restores.
MotoPass never stores or sees user documents — only the SHA-256 hash and metadata (name, size, type) are recorded.
A Satohash proof is cryptographic timestamp evidence, not a legal document — it proves data existed at a point in time.
The intel manifest's proof.in_sync field uses SHA-256 of the canonical slice (JSON.stringify with sorted keys) to detect drift.

hash_and_stamp: User enters text or uploads a file on /verify
Hash is submitted to POST /api/stamp with filename
API returns a stamp id (uuid) and status 'pending'
Client polls GET /api/stamps/:id until terminal status or 4 attempts
On confirmed: block height and confirmed_at are shown
User can optionally announce the stamp on Nostr via NIP-07
document_stamp_vault: User selects a file in the Vault Document Stamper
File is SHA-256 hashed locally (file never leaves device)
Hash is submitted to Satohash API
Stamp is polled for Bitcoin anchor
Registry entry is created/updated in localStorage
Entry appears across Profile, Vault, and Dashboard (shared registry)
re_anchor_programs: Daily intel pipeline detects data changes (probe, fetch, diff)
Changed canonical slices are re-hashed and re-stamped
Pacing: 2s delay, max 15 stamps per run
Old proofs preserved in audit_trail with source and hash
proof.in_sync updated to reflect current anchor state
batch_verify: User pastes multiple SHA-256 hashes (one per line)
Each hash gets a verify link to satohash.io/verify/<hash>
Results can be downloaded as JSON or all hashes copied
ots_file_verify: User uploads a .ots file or pastes hex/base64 content
Browser parses the binary content (structural check only)
Content is paired with an expected SHA-256 hash
Result indicates structural validity — full verify requires Satohash server
nostr_attestation: buildTimestampAttestationEvent() creates kind 30078 with sanitized tags
validateTimestampTemplate() ensures all tags are allowlisted
getEventHash() + verifyEvent() validate NIP-01 hash and Schnorr signature
Result includes relay summary and recovery status (published/signed-unpublished/stub/rejected)

stamp_lifecycle.pending: Submitted to Satohash API, awaiting Bitcoin block inclusion
stamp_lifecycle.confirmed: Bitcoin block height received — anchor is on-chain
stamp_lifecycle.error: API failure, polling timeout, or rejected — retry available

verify_modes.opentimestamps: Full OTS verification (requires server or Node CLI)
verify_modes.structural: Browser-side structural check of .ots binary content
verify_modes.hash-only: Valid 64-hex hash, not yet stamped or confirmed on Bitcoin
verify_modes.failed: Invalid input, parse error, or API rejection

nostr_recovery.published: Signed and accepted by at least one relay
nostr_recovery.signed-unpublished: Signed locally but no relay accepted — keep the JSON
nostr_recovery.stub: No NIP-07 extension available — unsigned copyable JSON
nostr_recovery.rejected: Template validation failed or signer returned a different event

honesty_rules: A hash alone is not proof — it must be anchored on Bitcoin via Satohash/OTS.
A .ots file uploaded to the browser is structurally checked only — full verification requires the Satohash server or opentimestamps CLI.
A Nostr post is an attestation, not proof — the Bitcoin anchor is the proof.
Demo proofs are placeholders for testing — never present them as verified.
The file never leaves the device — only the SHA-256 hash is submitted to the API.
Statuses are honest: pending means not yet confirmed; error means something failed.
Re-stamping after a data change is expected behavior — the old proof is not invalidated, a new one is created.
A stamp is cryptographic timestamp evidence, not a legal document or binding proof.

member_scripts.what_is_verify: Verification means checking that a SHA-256 hash matches its Bitcoin anchor on Satohash — proving the data existed unchanged since the stamp was created.
member_scripts.how_to_stamp: Go to /verify, paste or type your data, click Generate Hash, then click Stamp via Satohash. The API anchors your hash into Bitcoin via OpenTimestamps.
member_scripts.what_is_pending: Pending means the hash has been submitted to the Satohash API but a Bitcoin block has not yet included the anchor. It usually confirms within the hour.
member_scripts.what_is_confirmed: Confirmed means a Bitcoin block height has been recorded — your hash is immutably anchored on the Bitcoin blockchain.
member_scripts.can_i_verify_offline: You can paste a hash and check format, or upload a .ots file for structural validation. But full proof verification requires the Satohash API to be online.
member_scripts.what_is_ots: OpenTimestamps (OTS) is a protocol that batch-commits data hashes into Bitcoin transactions via calendar servers — Satohash wraps this into a simple API.
member_scripts.is_it_legally_binding: A Satohash proof is cryptographic timestamp evidence proving data existed at a point in time. It is not a legal document — consult legal counsel for binding agreements.
member_scripts.how_do_i_reverify: Your recent hashes are saved in the Hash History section on /verify. Click Re-verify to check any previous hash again, or visit satohash.io/verify/<hash> directly.

page_map./verify: Hash generation, Satohash stamping, OTS paste/file verify, batch verify, hash history
page_map./vault: Document Stamper (file → hash → stamp → registry), registry list, export/import
page_map./dashboard: Document registry card with stamp/re-check quick action, alert inbox
page_map./profile: Application status with stamped document status derived from registry
page_map./apply: Application hash generation and Satohash proof attachment
